The most important stock in most retirement accounts just lost its CEO.

Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after 33 years, effective immediately, amid an espionage scandal. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday, and three House committees want Huang in Washington on December 1.

If you own an S&P 500 index fund, you own Nvidia — it is one of the fund's largest holdings.

My take: one person built this company's story for three decades. Markets are about to find out how much of the price was the story.

Do you know what the biggest holding in your retirement fund is?

Source: Nvidia 8-K filing; CNBC, Nov 12, 2026

Educational only — not financial advice.

#Nvidia #Investing #RetirementSavings

A rate hike in December is now almost fully priced in.

October consumer prices rose 0.4%, hotter than forecast. Core inflation has run 0.3% a month for three straight months. Markets price a 99% chance the Fed raises rates to 4.00%–4.25% on December 9 — and Fed governor Christopher Waller says a double-size half-point hike should be considered.

Credit card APRs and new loan rates follow within weeks. Savings yields follow too — the one upside.

My take: borrowing through the holidays is about to get more expensive, and most people will not notice until the January statement.

What would one more rate hike change for you?

Source: BLS CPI, October 2026; CME FedWatch via Benzinga

#Inflation #InterestRates #Fed

America is buying homes at 2010 speed — with 30 million more people.

Existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October to an annual pace of 3.75 million, the lowest since August 2010, the National Association of Realtors reported November 12. Mortgage rates averaged 7.33% in October, the highest since 2000 outside one month in 2023. The median home sold for $416,700. Unsold supply is the highest in about 11 years.

My take: sellers have finally shown up, and the buyers who waited years for inventory now can't afford the rate.

Are you waiting on prices, or waiting on rates?

Source: NAR Existing-Home Sales, October 2026

#HousingMarket #MortgageRates #RealEstate

Bitcoin is having its worst stretch of the year.

It broke below $68,000 Saturday, down more than 20% since late October and heading for a sixth straight weekly loss. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have bled money for seven straight trading days — $1.9 billion out since November 5.

One research firm estimates the average ETF buyer paid around $81,000 per coin. On that math, the average buyer is underwater.

My take: the ETFs were sold as the easy on-ramp. Nobody advertised that the exit uses the same door.

Does a 20% drop change how you think about crypto in a retirement mix?

Source: SoSoValue/Farside data via Investing.com, Nov 14, 2026

Educational only — not financial advice.

Finally, a number at the pump moving your way.

The national average fell to $3.98 a gallon this week, AAA reports — down from $4.33 a month ago. Until this fall, the average had never even been above $4 in November.

It is still about a dollar more than a year ago. The drop comes from falling demand after the driving season, while crude prices remain high.

My take: enjoy it, but this is seasonal relief, not a fix — the price of oil hasn't surrendered anything.

What are you paying per gallon where you live?

Source: AAA national average, Nov 10, 2026

#GasPrices #CostOfLiving #Energy

Update on the largest theft in history.

The Justice Department said Thursday it has seized about $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance, with more than $2.7 billion of the $6 billion total now frozen. The FBI attributes the October 29 hack to North Korean military hackers it calls TraderTraitor.

The stolen coins were scattered across roughly 12,000 wallets in over 40,000 transactions — a new wallet every 25 seconds, per CSIS.

Binance says customers lost nothing. Researchers say much of the rest may never be recovered.

My take: an exchange is only as safe as its least careful employee's laptop.

Do you keep coins on an exchange or in your own wallet?

Source: DOJ; FBI; CSIS, Nov 2026

#Crypto #CyberSecurity #Binance
column6: Source: U.S. Justice Department; FBI, Nov 13, 2026 — https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/13/us-seizes-binance-hack-crypto.html

The newest cyberattacks don't steal data. They spoil food.

Since the summer, suspected Iranian hackers have locked operators out of small-town water stations across the Midwest and breached systems on two Texas-bound energy tankers, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday. In Europe, grocery-store refrigerators were remotely cranked to 120 degrees, spoiling tons of food. French blood banks were targeted too.

Attribution is still under investigation — officials say suspected, not proven.

The bill lands where it always does: grocery prices, water bills, insurance premiums.

My take: we connected everything to the internet to save money, and the savings are now the attack surface.

Would you hear about it if your town's water system was hacked?

Source: The Wall Street Journal, Nov 13, 2026

#CyberSecurity #FoodPrices #Infrastructure
column6: Source: The Wall Street Journal, Nov 13, 2026 — https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/iran-expands-cyberattacks-greater-real-132640639.html

The biggest IPO in history is days away.

Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, prices Wednesday and starts trading Thursday on the Nasdaq as ANT. The range: $70 to $78 a share, valuing it as high as $1.45 trillion and raising up to $64 billion — more than twice any IPO before it. About 20% of shares are reserved for retail investors, far above the usual.

The other side of the ledger: the company is deeply unprofitable, and AI stocks have sold off hard this month.

My take: a 20% retail slice means regular people get the first-day price — and the first-day risk. Those arrive together.

Would you ever buy a stock on day one?

Source: Anthropic amended S-1; CNBC, Nov 10, 2026

Educational only — not financial advice.

A $3.7 trillion question is hanging over Tesla.

Tesla and SpaceX have formed committees to explore a merger — a combination Bloomberg values near $3.7 trillion, which would make it the largest corporate deal ever attempted. Bloomberg also calculates that a change of control could vest more than $110 billion of Musk's Tesla shares.

No deal has been announced. Tesla shareholders would have to approve one, and the annual meeting is December 3.

My take: when one person stands on both sides of a $3.7 trillion deal, the fine print matters more than the vision.

If your index fund votes your Tesla shares, do you know how?

Source: Bloomberg; Tesla statements, Oct–Nov 2026

Educational only — not financial advice.

#Tesla #SpaceX #ElonMusk

Here's something that got almost no coverage this week.

The October CPI report has no annual inflation rate. Last fall's government shutdown stopped price collection for October 2025 — and with no year-ago data, no 12-month comparison can be calculated now.

The annual rate is expected back on December 10. The Fed decides interest rates on December 9 — one day before.

So the most quoted inflation number in America is simply missing, at the exact moment it matters most.

My take: every paycheck negotiation, lease renewal and benefit adjustment leans on that number. Its absence is a real cost, just an invisible one.

Did you know this number was missing?

Source: BLS CPI release, October 2026

#Inflation #Economy #CPI
